# Somatic Loss of the Y Chromosome (LOY) in Cancer

Somatic loss of the Y chromosome (LOY) is the most common human sex-chromosome aneuploidy, occurring both as age-associated mosaicism in peripheral leukocytes (`mLOY`) and as a frequent clonal or subclonal somatic alteration across male solid tumours and haematological malignancies. In pan-cancer genomic cohorts such as The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), LOY spans a wide prevalence gradient—exceeding 40–75% in papillary renal cell carcinoma (`KIRP`), oesophageal carcinoma (`ESCA`), head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (`HNSC`), bladder urothelial carcinoma (`BLCA`), and lung squamous/adenocarcinoma (`LUSC`/`LUAD`)—and correlates with shorter progression-free or overall survival in multiple tumour types.

Despite its clinical prevalence, two fundamental questions have remained unresolved in the cancer genomics literature:

1. **What are the direct, cell-intrinsic transcriptional and chromatin consequences of losing chromosome Y?** Published studies have reported seemingly contradictory phenotypes—ranging from extensive epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling, and immune evasion in clonal models (Abdel-Hafiz et al., 2023; Celli et al., 2024; Dorsch et al., 2026; Schlüter et al., 2026) to minimal autosomal transcriptional perturbation beyond sex-chromosome dosage in renal cell carcinoma (Waterhölter et al., 2026). Because prior experimental models relied on single-cell cloning, spontaneous sublines, or constitutively integrated Cas9 vectors, subclonal copy-number drift and clonal selection bottlenecks have confounded the direct effect of Y loss.
2. **Which genetic and pharmacological vulnerabilities are selectively exposed by LOY?** While correlative analyses of heterogeneous cell-line panels (DepMap, Project Score) consistently recover four X-linked paralog dependencies (*DDX3X*, *EIF1AX*, *RPS4X*, and *ZFX*), whether LOY also generates context-specific dependencies in chromatin coactivator, transcriptional, or metabolic modules—and why such hits do not emerge in stratified public cohorts—has lacked systematic investigation in matched isogenic genomes.

---

# Architecture of the Human Y Chromosome (`T2T-CHM13v2.0`)

The complete telomere-to-telomere human Y assembly (`T2T-CHM13v2.0` / HG002, 62.46 Mb) resolves both pseudoautosomal regions (`PAR1` at the distal Yp tip, ~2.77 Mb; `PAR2` at the distal Yq tip, ~330 kb) and the male-specific region of the Y (`MSY`), which comprises:

- **Euchromatic `Yp` and `Yq11`:** Houses single-copy X-degenerate genes (the ancestral X–Y gametologs) alongside ampliconic gene families (*TSPY* tandem array on Yp; *RBMY*, *DAZ*, *CDY* across palindromes P1–P8 on Yq).
- **Centromeric `DYZ3` ($\alpha$-satellite) and heterochromatic `Yq12` (`DYZ1` / `HSat3` and `DYZ2`):** Massive repetitive arrays that provide high-copy target substrates for programmable Cas9 cleavage without cutting autosomes or the X chromosome.

Crucially, because standard short-read reference genomes include identical `PAR1` and `PAR2` sequences on both chrX and chrY, unmasked alignments discard multimapping PAR reads (`MAPQ = 0`). Throughout this repository (Chapters 3 and 4), both `lpWGS` and `STAR v2` RNA-seq pipelines use **Y-PAR-masked references** so that all pseudoautosomal reads map uniquely to the X-coordinate PAR intervals while preserving male-specific Y (`MSY`) quantification.

---

# The X–Y Gametolog Buffering Problem

Twelve ubiquitous X-degenerate MSY genes pair with non-inactivated (XCI-escaping) paralogs on the X chromosome that perform conserved housekeeping functions in translation, RNA splicing, transcription, deubiquitination, and histone demethylation:

| Y-linked Gametolog | X-linked Paralog | Regional Location | Core Molecular Function |
|---|---|---|---|
| *RPS4Y1* | *RPS4X* | Distal Yp (~2.54 Mb, proximal to `PAR1`) | 40S ribosomal subunit protein eS4 |
| *ZFY* | *ZFX* | Distal Yp (~2.93 Mb) | C2H2 zinc-finger transcription factor |
| *TBL1Y* | *TBL1X* | Yp (~6.91 Mb) | NCoR/SMRT corepressor WD40 subunit |
| *USP9Y* | *USP9X* | Proximal Yq11 (~12.71 Mb) | Deubiquitinating peptidase (DUB) |
| *DDX3Y* | *DDX3X* | Proximal Yq11 (~12.91 Mb) | DEAD-box ATP-dependent RNA helicase; translation initiation |
| *UTY* (*KDM6C*) | *KDM6A* (*UTX*) | Proximal Yq11 (~13.23 Mb) | TPR/JmjC chromatin regulator; COMPASS/BAF scaffolding & phase separation |
| *TMSB4Y* | *TMSB4X* | Yq11 (~13.70 Mb) | Actin-monomer sequestering peptide |
| *NLGN4Y* | *NLGN4X* | Yq11 (~14.52 Mb) | Synaptic / cell-surface adhesion protein |
| *PRKY* | *PRKX* | Yp (~7.27 Mb) | cAMP-dependent serine/threonine kinase |
| *KDM5D* (*JARID1D*) | *KDM5C* (*JARID1C*) | Euchromatic Yq11 (~19.70 Mb) | JmjC H3K4me2/3 demethylase; PRC1.6/NuRD/Sin3 interactors |
| *TXLNGY* (*CYorf15B*) | *TXLNG* | Yq11 (~19.56 Mb) | Taxilin syntaxin-binding family (pseudogene on Y) |
| *EIF1AY* | *EIF1AX* | Distal euchromatic Yq11 (~20.58 Mb) | Translation initiation factor eIF1A (43S pre-initiation complex) |

Across HT1080, A549, and DU145, losing chromosome Y eliminates or depletes Y-linked gametolog expression **without triggering compensatory transcriptional upregulation of their X-linked paralogs** (Chapter 3, §3.3.3.4). Consequently, total combined X+Y gametolog dosage drops directly upon Y loss, exposing cells to synthetic lethality when the remaining X-linked paralog is inhibited or knocked out.

At the same time, our structural characterization reveals that Cas9 cleavage of Y repeats does not always eliminate the entire chromosome: while A549 undergoes whole-Y loss, HT1080 and especially DU145 completely lose euchromatic `Yq` (*USP9Y*–*EIF1AY*) and proximal `Yp` (*AMELY* at ~6.5 Mb) while partially retaining a distal male-specific `Yp` block (~2.46–4.80 Mb) encoding *RPS4Y1* and *ZFY*. This regional retention explains why single-locus *AMELY*/*AMELX* assays misclassify partial Y deletions as complete LOY and directly impacts which X–Y paralogs score as synthetic lethal in downstream screens.

# Central Thesis Hypotheses and Experimental Framework

The thesis is organized around three linked investigations (Chapters 2–4):

| Thesis Chapter | Central Question & Approach | Repository Modules |
|---|---|---|
| **Chapter 2** (*npj Syst Biol Appl* 2025) | Can pan-cancer integration of DepMap CRISPR screens, TCGA mutual exclusivity, and PRISM drug profiling identify clinically actionable synthetic lethalities—and do small molecules phenocopy knockout of their nominal targets? | Contextual foundation; LOY extension in [`01_depmap_prism_public/`](01_depmap_prism_public/) |
| **Chapter 3** (Isogenic LOY Models & Multi-Omic Profiling) | Can transient repeat-targeting Cas9 RNP delivery generate pooled, clone-free isogenic LOY models across cancer lineages, and what are the conserved versus lineage-specific transcriptional, chromatin-accessibility, and *UTY*/*KDM5D*-reversible consequences of Y depletion? | [`02_genome_engineering/`](02_genome_engineering/) · [`03_rnaseq_transcriptomics/`](03_rnaseq_transcriptomics/) · [`04_atacseq_chromatin/`](04_atacseq_chromatin/) · [`05_uty_kdm5d_addback/`](05_uty_kdm5d_addback/) |
| **Chapter 4** (Public Cohort Power Limits, Isogenic CRISPR Screens & Competition Validation) | Why do public panels recover only four X–Y gametologs, what paralog and non-paralog dependencies (including SAGA, Mediator, and sterol/selenoprotein pathways) emerge in matched isogenic Brunello CRISPR screens, how specific are they across 27 external isogenic screens, and do top candidates validate in reciprocal spectral competition assays? | [`01_depmap_prism_public/`](01_depmap_prism_public/) · [`06_crispr_screens/`](06_crispr_screens/) · [`07_competitive_growth_assays/`](07_competitive_growth_assays/) |

# Key Mechanistic Conclusions

1. **Absence of X-paralog compensation and practical rules of gametolog synthetic lethality:** Y loss reduces summed `PAR1` expression by 23–33% and removes Yq gametologs without X-paralog transcriptional compensation. In genome-wide CRISPR screens, which X–Y gametolog scores depends on (i) **parental baseline dependency and Y dosage** (HT1080 is tolerant of *DDX3X* loss at baseline [`Chronos +0.18`], unmasking *DDX3X* at `normZ = -11.45`, whereas parental A549 already depends strongly on *DDX3X* [`Chronos -0.98`] and instead recovers *EIF1AX*), (ii) **pre-D0 dropout kinetics** of pan-essential housekeeping genes (*EIF1AX*, *RPS4X*), and (iii) **regional Yp retention** (*RPS4Y1*, *ZFY*).
2. **Lineage-dependent autosomal rewiring vs. conserved cell-intrinsic interferon suppression:** Pairwise autosomal gene-level fold-change correlations across HT1080, DU145, and A549 are near zero ($\rho = -0.06$ to $0.11$), reconciling why different tumour lineages display distinct gene-level programmes (e.g., *GRHL2* and luminal epithelial suppression in DU145 vs. mesenchymal/synaptic/ECM remodelling in HT1080). At the pathway level, however, type I and type II interferon and inflammatory signalling are recurrently suppressed across our models and 18 external Y-loss/mosaic datasets—demonstrating a cell-intrinsic innate immune dampening effect of Y depletion.
3. **Promoter chromatin closing at Polycomb targets and causal *UTY* rescue:** Rather than causing global Polycomb derepression, Y depletion in HT1080 drives an ~7:1 skew toward chromatin closing (663 closed vs. 95 opened ATAC-seq peaks), with jointly closed and downregulated promoters significantly enriched for PRC2 (*EZH2*/*SUZ12*) and H3K27me3 occupancy after matching for baseline accessibility, GC content, and CpG density. Lentiviral re-expression of *UTY* (alone or with *KDM5D*), but not *KDM5D* alone, partially reverses the 150-gene (51% / 35%) and frozen-100-gene LOY transcriptional signatures and increases expression at 36 of 39 jointly closed/repressed genes.
4. **Coactivator (SAGA / Mediator) and metabolic vulnerabilities beyond X–Y paralogs:** In HT1080, Y depletion creates coordinated sensitivity to knockout of six of 20 SAGA subunits (*TAF6L*, *TADA2B*, *SUPT20H*, *ATXN7L3*, *TADA1*, *TAF5L*), Mediator (*MED12*), and SREBP sterol/selenoprotein pathways (*SREBF2*, *SREBF1*, *SCLY*, *ACSL4*). Multi-omic integration proves these vulnerabilities are not driven by transcriptional silencing or promoter closure of the candidate genes themselves ($\rho = -0.005$), and cross-screen benchmarking across 27 external isogenic CRISPR screens shows that while *DDX3X* dependency is strictly unique to LOY, SAGA sensitization represents a convergent coactivator vulnerability shared with select aneuploid (13q loss) and oncogenic (*KEAP1*-mutant) states.
